hyperedges.label: Route Leg Structure Drives Every Scene Reading
Legacy prototype stage walkthrough and autoplay flow

nodes.label: Vanishing Contaminant Specks
nodes.description: 16 brown jittered spheres that ride in with the raw water and fade out at a random vanishAt fraction between 0.12 and 0.58 of the route, standing in for a filter stage catching them. Precursor of grit caught at the first element.

nodes.label: Constant-speed Water Pulses
nodes.description: 28 small spheres evenly spaced in phase along the single service-line curve, all advancing at the same speed (0.11 per second) regardless of stage, coloured by colorAt. Precursor of the time-spaced bubble column.

nodes.label: colorAt()
nodes.description: Piecewise-linear lookup of colorStops for a route parameter t, returning a lerped THREE.Color.

nodes.label: animate()
nodes.description: requestAnimationFrame loop: clamps delta to 50 ms, ticks the orbit rig, advances pulses along the curve at a constant speed and tints them via colorAt, moves two glow lights with pulses 0 and 4, advances jittered contaminants until their vanishAt fade, pulses the tap stream opacity and cycles the glass fill every 7 s, then renders.

nodes.label: buildScene()
nodes.description: Builds the whole three.js scene: renderer (pixel ratio capped at 2), fog, lights, grid, box house with extruded roof, service-line CatmullRomCurve3 tube from street meter to tap, three canisters, tap glass, pulses, contaminants, glow point lights, tap stream and filling glass; creates the orbit rig, wires raycast picking to selectStage, and starts the animate loop.

nodes.label: stopAutoplay()
nodes.description: Clears the autoplay interval and restores the play icon.

nodes.label: addCanister()
nodes.description: Creates one stage canister (transmissive glass shell, emissive core, invisible sphere hit target) at a route point, registers the meshes as pickables with a stageKey, and records stagePositions and stageCores for that stage.

nodes.label: tweenTo()
nodes.description: Cubic ease-out fly-to over requestAnimationFrame: lerps target, radius and optionally theta/phi over a duration (default 850 ms). No angle normalisation, so laps of auto-rotate unwind on reset.

nodes.label: makeOrbit()
nodes.description: Drag-to-orbit camera rig factory: spherical theta/phi/radius state, pointer drag with a click-vs-drag threshold (moved < 6 px fires _onClickPick), wheel zoom clamped to min/max radius, auto-rotate after 2.2 s idle, and returns tick/focus/reset/setClickHandler.

nodes.label: orbit.focus()
nodes.description: Flies the camera target to a position at a given radius, leaving theta/phi untouched.

nodes.label: colorStops
nodes.description: Hard-coded colour stops along route parameter t (amber raw -> grey after sediment -> cyan after carbon -> mint at output) with abrupt 2-3% transitions at fixed fractions rather than across the element spans.

nodes.label: Dark Navy Glass UI Theme
nodes.description: Inline CSS theme: navy-deep background with radial cyan/azure glows, translucent backdrop-blurred panels, fixed cyan accent, mint/amber for after/before values, floating pointer-events:none cards over the canvas, pill play bar and responsive hiding of trend/impact cards under 760px.

nodes.label: roDotLabel
nodes.description: Label of the third stage dot per system: Minerals / RO / UV.

nodes.label: filtration-simulation.html
nodes.description: Original single-file prototype kept verbatim: inline CSS dark theme, hand-written DOM UI (sidebar, floating cards, play bar, stage dots) and a three.js r128 scene loaded from cdnjs with a global-script orbit rig, a single CatmullRom service line, three canisters and a tap, water pulses and contaminant specks. Wires DOM events at load: window load -> buildScene + selectStage('carbon').

nodes.label: orbit.tick()
nodes.description: Per-frame rig update: accumulates idle time and auto-rotates theta when not dragging after 2.2 s.

nodes.label: stageDataBySystem
nodes.description: Per-system (whole / undersink / rain) title and description copy for each of the four stages.

nodes.label: systemData
nodes.description: Per-system header title/subtitle and the cost-before/after/savings and bottles/waste figures shown in the floating cards.

nodes.label: updateCamera()
nodes.description: Places the camera on the sphere defined by theta/phi/radius around the target and calls lookAt.

nodes.label: selectStage()
nodes.description: Sets currentStage, writes the detail card, stage count and progress width from stageDataBySystem/stageOrder, toggles the active stage dot, raises the selected canister core's emissiveIntensity (0.9 vs 0.28) and, unless skipZoom, flies the orbit rig to stagePositions[key].

nodes.label: selectSystem()
nodes.description: Sets currentSystem, toggles the active sidebar button, writes header and card figures from systemData, relabels the RO dot, stops autoplay, resets the camera and re-applies the current stage without zooming. The 3D scene itself does not change per system in the prototype.

nodes.label: startAutoplay()
nodes.description: Swaps the play icon to pause and advances to the next stage in stageOrder every 3200 ms via selectStage.

nodes.label: Space Grotesk and Inter Google Fonts
nodes.description: The design's type pairing, loaded from fonts.googleapis.com in weights 400-700: Space Grotesk for display and headings, Inter for body. The same stylesheet URL is used by both the Vite entry and the legacy prototype.
nodes.norm_label: space grotesk and inter google fonts

nodes.label: orbit.reset()
nodes.description: Tweens back to the initial target, default radius, theta and phi over 800 ms.

nodes.label: index.html
nodes.description: Vite entry page: sets the viewport (viewport-fit=cover), preconnects to Google Fonts, loads Space Grotesk and Inter, and mounts the React app at #root via /src/main.jsx.

nodes.label: stageOrder
nodes.description: ['sediment','carbon','ro','tap'] - the four stage keys in walkthrough order.

nodes.label: NOTE: `moved` is intentionally left alone here. It is reset on
nodes.norm_label: note: `moved` is intentionally left alone here. it is reset on

nodes.label: Roof and Front Wall Cutaway
nodes.rationale: The under-sink view fades the roof and front wall away so the camera can get into the kitchen; Reset view puts everything back.

nodes.label: Rainwater System
nodes.rationale: Stainless three-canister unit with UV lamp and gauges on top, placed on the right gable wall beside the rainwater tank.

nodes.label: Under Sink System
nodes.rationale: Three-canister RO unit plus pressure tank and a dedicated tap, placed inside the kitchen sink cabinet.

nodes.label: Whole House System
nodes.rationale: White point-of-entry cabinet with copper riser and ball valve, placed on the front wall where the mains comes in from the street meter.

nodes.label: X-Ray Reveal
nodes.rationale: Selecting a system makes the unit's cover, cartridge housings and the pipework the route runs inside go see-through so the water is visible for the whole journey rather than only where it crosses open ground.

nodes.label: FadeGroup needsUpdate
nodes.rationale: FadeGroup flips material.transparent at runtime; three bakes that flag into the compiled shader, so it sets needsUpdate when the flag changes. Without it a material that started opaque stays opaque regardless of opacity.

nodes.label: Revealed Pipework Thinning
nodes.rationale: A product whose route runs inside modelled pipework should thin that pipework out on revealed, as the three existing units do; otherwise the water is hidden inside its own plumbing for most of the journey.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph
nodes.rationale: Persistent graph at graphify-out/ with god nodes, community structure and cross-file relationships; graphify-out/wiki/index.md is preferred for broad navigation over raw source browsing, and GRAPH_REPORT.md is reserved for broad architecture review.

nodes.label: Graphify Update After Code Change
nodes.rationale: Run `graphify update .` after modifying code so the graph stays current; it is AST-only and costs no API calls.

nodes.label: Query-First Rule
nodes.rationale: For codebase questions run graphify query / path / explain before reading raw files, because they return a scoped subgraph that is usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output.

nodes.label: Keyboard Tour Controls
nodes.rationale: Space plays and pauses; the arrow keys step between stages; Home and End go to the first and last stage.

nodes.label: Scrubbable Progress Bar
nodes.rationale: The progress bar is the playhead: click or drag anywhere and the tour goes there, landing on the stage that point falls in. Its colours are the water's own per-stage list, raw at the left and finished at the right, so the bar is the journey in miniature with a hairline at each stage boundary.

nodes.label: Stage Seek Keeps Tour State
nodes.rationale: Picking a stage from the dots, keyboard or scene seeks: the tour moves there and keeps whatever state it had, so a paused tour can be stepped stage by stage with the water held at each. Switching system or resetting the view ends the tour.

nodes.label: Hand-Written Orbit Rig
nodes.rationale: The camera is a custom rig (useOrbitRig), not drei's OrbitControls: the click-vs-drag threshold and the fly-to tween with angle normalisation (so it never unwinds laps of auto-rotate) are load-bearing for the interaction.

nodes.label: Pause as Freeze-Frame
nodes.rationale: Pause stops the playhead and the water together (bubbles held mid-cartridge, grit held on the element face) while the camera stays free, so a paused tour can be orbited and inspected. UI motion that is not simulation (fly-to in flight, route highlight sliding on, badges tinting) still settles.

nodes.label: Playhead Written Straight to DOM
nodes.rationale: The play bar's playhead is written directly to the DOM as a CSS variable that both the fill and the knob read, from a subscription on the walkthrough. Holding it in React state would re-render the app, canvas included, every frame.

nodes.label: Real-Time Clocks with Stall Cap
nodes.rationale: The walkthrough's clock and the water's clock are the exception to damping: they must keep real time, so they take the frame's whole delta capped at a quarter second rather than 0.05. The cap only swallows a stall (background tab, shader compile); a machine merely struggling still gets a tour that runs to time and water at the right speed. Both clocks read a paused flag rather than being torn down, so resuming is just letting the delta count again.

nodes.label: Resume Honours Remaining Dwell
nodes.rationale: Resume carries on from the same instant for both the tour and the water; the remainder of the current stage is honoured rather than restarted.

nodes.label: Walkthrough as a Timeline
nodes.rationale: The play button runs a looping guided tour of the four stages, 3.2 seconds each. It is a timeline rather than a timer: one playhead in seconds, and the stage showing is whichever dwell the playhead is inside. That is what makes Play, Pause and Resume honest. Play starts at the stage on screen and flies the camera straight in instead of waiting at the wide view for the first stage change.

nodes.label: Grit Capture
nodes.rationale: Specks riding in with the raw water are each given a point on the face of the first element to stop at, biased toward the leading edge, and sit there a moment before fading.

nodes.label: Route Legs
nodes.rationale: Each system's route is authored as a chain of legs (one pipe run each) tagged with stage, whether it passes through a filter element, pace, and whether it is buried. Every leg boundary is a real control point of the curve, so each stage's span along the path is measured rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Route Line
nodes.rationale: A thin line traces the whole path carrying the same gradient, faint where the run is buried and lit along the selected stage. It is thinner than the narrowest pipe it runs inside, so it shows only in the gaps: buried runs and inside the cartridges.

nodes.label: Adding a Product Checklist
nodes.rationale: Adding a product: a mount point in layout.js, a view / stages / legs entry in systems.js, copy in data/constants.js, a component under three/products/, and render it in Scene.jsx with unitProps(key).

nodes.label: Colour Ramp Across Element
nodes.rationale: The water colour ramp sits across each filter element so a bubble visibly clears while it is working through the cartridge instead of changing colour once it is already out the far side.

nodes.label: Single media Leg Declaration
nodes.rationale: Write legs in flow order, each listing only the points it adds. Marking the run through each filter element media: true with a slow pace is the one declaration that places the colour change, the stage marker and the slowdown. buried: true draws the route line faintly where a run disappears underground or under the floor.

nodes.label: Time-Spaced Bubble Column
nodes.rationale: Bubbles are spaced evenly in time rather than distance so they crowd through media and the pressure tank and spread out in open pipe, and can never overtake one another. Each rides at its own offset from the centreline and turns slowly around it so the column churns, and stretches along its travel direction in proportion to speed. Every system takes the same ten seconds end to end regardless of how much of the route is slow.

nodes.label: Water Clock at useFrame Priority -1
nodes.rationale: The water's clock is stepped in a useFrame at priority -1 so it is ahead of the bubbles and grit that read it in the same frame. r3f runs frame callbacks in priority order; only a priority above zero switches off automatic render, so a negative priority is safe purely for ordering.

nodes.label: House Cladding Wood Texture
nodes.description: Flat, evenly-lit photo texture of light natural oak wood grain, roughly 900x650px landscape. Warm honey/pale-tan colour with low contrast, horizontal grain running left-to-right, subtle cathedral figure in the upper half and a few small dark knots. No visible plank seams, bevels or shadow gradients, so it reads as a single continuous wood surface rather than pre-composed cladding boards; tiling suitability is moderate (horizontal repeat is plausible, vertical repeat may show the cathedral figure). Intended as the timber/cladding albedo map for the cabin walls in the diorama.

nodes.label: Base Colour Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Surfaces are base colours only. Timber (deck, floor, window frames) is the obvious candidate for textures later; the cladding could take a vertical-board normal map.

nodes.label: Timber Cladding Material
nodes.rationale: The diorama direction is a light product-render cabin with base colours only, where the user textures timber themselves; this light oak texture is the swappable colour map for the cabin's exterior cladding, chosen for its warm low-contrast tone that stays readable under simple PCF shadows without competing with the water-filtration focus.

nodes.label: Light Theme Accent Switch
nodes.rationale: styles/index.css is a light theme whose accent colour is switched by the data-system attribute on .app; picking a system switches the UI accent.

nodes.label: Stage Badges
nodes.rationale: A numbered badge hangs at each of the four stages, anchored to the middle of that stage's element; the selected one takes the accent colour and grows. Past a few metres the unselected badges fade so the wide view carries one 'you are here' pin rather than four overlapping discs.

nodes.label: UI Chrome Over Canvas
nodes.rationale: The UI chrome is plain React and CSS layered over the canvas; none of it is drawn inside Three.js.

nodes.label: Fill-Rate Budget
nodes.rationale: The scene is fill-rate bound, not geometry bound: halving resolution roughly doubles frame rate. So dpr is capped at 1.5 rather than 2 and the rim light does not cast shadows; on integrated graphics at 1600x1000 the pair take a high-DPI display from about 12fps to about 24. Smooth motion matters more because water that stutters stops reading as water. Measure before re-enabling either.

nodes.label: Frame-Rate Independent Damping
nodes.rationale: Anything animated per frame damps with Math.min(1, delta * rate), never a fixed per-frame fraction; otherwise transitions run at different speeds on different monitors and look broken rather than slow on a slow machine. Transitions cap delta at 0.05.

nodes.label: Hard-Edge Outline
nodes.rationale: The active unit is outlined with its own hard edges in the accent colour rather than an inverted hull. The hull was tried first but depends on the object writing depth, and these units stop writing depth once the x-ray fades their covers; stencil masking still left a wide fringe. Edges sit exactly on the surface so they behave the same whether the cover is solid or see-through. Drawn via drei's Line, not lineSegments, because WebGL clamps native line width to one pixel.
